title: Excellence
hook: doing a job well is a form of love
tomorrow: who carries the other corners when the work gets heavy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, work shares in creation: a job in the garden before anything went wrong. The line was co-creators.

Two coworkers set up the same bakery case. One redoes the display until every row is perfect, and the line waits. The other rushes it, smiles at every customer, and leaves crumbs on the glass. Which one did the job well? Customers would probably split. Catholic tradition has two strong answers, and they pull against each other in a useful way.
screen: `TWO COWORKERS, ONE CASE.` → `PERFECT ROWS, OR A WARM SMILE?` → `TWO STRONG ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: The first voice says the craft matters. In the parable of the talents, the master doesn't praise good intentions. He praises servants who actually traded and doubled what they were given: "Well done, good and faithful servant." And when the crowd in Mark watches Jesus heal a deaf man, their verdict is about the work itself: "He hath done all things well." On this view, sloppy work isn't humble. It's careless with the people who'll use it, and a shoddy thing is a poor gift to God. The second voice says love comes first. Paul writes that if he gave away everything he owned to feed the poor and had not charity, it would profit him nothing. Saint Thérèse of Lisieux called her path the little way: small, hidden things done for love, where nobody is grading. On this view, chasing perfect can turn into pride, and God looks at the heart before the finish. Both voices agree on one thing: the work is for someone. The craft voice says love shows up in the details. The love voice says details without love are empty.
screen: `THE CRAFT VOICE: WELL DONE.` · `HE HATH DONE ALL THINGS WELL.` · `THE LOVE VOICE: THE LITTLE WAY.` · `THE WORK IS FOR SOMEONE.` · then, large: `WELL DONE.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write down one piece of your work from this week that went out a little rough: an email, a shift, an assignment, a meal. Under it, write one small thing that would make it better for the person who receives it.
Excellence. A job done well, as a form of love for whoever it's for.
Keep this one: well done, the small details as love made visible. Until tomorrow, then.

chat.meaning: The tradition holds both: 'well done, good and faithful servant' praises real work, and Paul says without charity it profits nothing.
